transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-04-10 14:00 PST; Duration: ~47m; Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Janelle (CSM), Sarah (CTO - Lakeside), Daniel (Head Sec), Priya (SRE), Ben (Legal)

Summary: quick review of compliance docs and deep dive into incident response, BCDR, RTO/RPO numbers, and escalation. Customer asked about SLA and how Redwood falls back across Dedicated/Hosted/Private deployments.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time, quick intros — I'm Maya on the account team, with Omar our solutions eng and Janelle on success.
[00:10] Sarah: hi all, Sarah from Lakeside, Daniel's with me and Priya, Ben from legal will drop in a bit. We're focused on incident response for anything that affects customer-facing banking flows.
[00:25] Omar: great, high level we'll cover our SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC and SSO options (SAML/Okta), audit logs and retention, plus the BCDR/IR runbook - RTO/RPO and escalation. happy to jump into technical details.
[00:40] Daniel: useful, want to be explicit about targets. We're looking for 99.95-ish uptime for core inference paths and RTO under 30 minutes for full failover, RPO less than 5 mins for transaction-affecting caches.
[00:55] Maya: noted. our public SLA for hosted is 99.9 but for Dedicated we can negotiate tighter commitments via reserved capacity contracts, and realistic RTO/RPO depends on deployment model and caching.
[01:15] Omar: quick caveat — if you use private on-prem with our package, you control much of the network, so RTO becomes a co-managed exercise. for hosted/dedicated we provide documented failover, automated routing, and warm standby options.
[01:40] Priya: can you describe what warm standby looks like? specifically how KV cache and prefix cache are handled — we can't accept minutes of cold-Warm cache rebuild.
[01:55] Omar: yeah, good question, our runtime supports prefix/KV cache snapshotting and transfer across nodes, we persist KV checkpoints to durable storage in S3 (or your objectstore in VPC) and we can replay to warm standby. typical restart + priming time depends on sequence length distribution; in practice for our banking customers we target <15 minutes for service-ready state but not fully primed model cache. that's why RTO definitions often distinguish service availability vs full performance.
[02:35] Daniel: so you separate availability RTO vs perf RTO. our ask is availability <10m, perf degraded acceptable up to 60m, but we need RPO for data / request logs to be sub-5m.
[02:50] Omar: that's reasonable, we'll map that in the runbook. note that RPO for request logs depends on region replication and retention settings. if you want cross-region sync <5m we can enable multi-region replication in Dedicated/Private setups.
[03:10] Sarah: what about encryption and key management? we need BYOK and HSM-backed KMS.
[03:20] Maya: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options via our private deployment. you can revoke keys, and we provide audit logs of key usage.
[03:35] Daniel: are audit logs immutable? retention windows? we have to satisfy audit committee and regulators.
[03:45] Omar: our audit logs are write-once, stored in tamper-evident storage with option to forward to your SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) or to an S3 bucket in your account. retention configurable, default 90 days; we can provide extended retention as an add-on to 1 year+ for compliance.
[04:05] Ben: legal question — if you store logs in our cloud account, what's the e-discovery path, and can Redwood access them?
[04:15] Maya: if logs are in your account, Redwood does not have direct access; we provide ingestion pipelines and read-only cross-account roles only when explicitly granted for troubleshooting. we'll include details in the security pack.
[04:30] [Speaker 1]: (mumble) also need SSO and RBAC details — how fine-grained?
[04:40] Omar: RBAC is role-based with least-privilege roles: admin/operator/audit/viewer. We integrate with SAML IdPs (Okta, Azure AD) and SCIM for provisioning. You can map groups to roles and enforce 2FA.
[04:58] Priya: can scoped API keys be limited to read-only for observability teams? we need separation of duty.
[05:05] Maya: yes, scoped API keys and token-level permissions exist; we'll share the permission matrix.
[05:20] Daniel: escalation — who do we call outside business hours? what's the on-call rotation?
[05:30] Omar: we have 24/7 escalation for severity 1 incidents for Dedicated and Private customers with premium SLA. On-call is a tiered model: first-line Redwood support, second-line infra on-call, third-line engineering. We'll provide a contact matrix with escalation times (e.g., 15m initial ack for Sev1).
[05:50] Sarah: show me an example runbook for a model-serving outage.
[06:00] Omar: sure — high level steps: detection (metrics/alerts), triage (isolate model vs infra), failover (route to warm standby or compatible model), cache priming, customer notif, and postmortem. We have templates. I'll walk through an example:
[06:20] [06:20] Omar: Step 1: alert triggers with 5xx rate > 1% and median latency spike. Step 2: check node health, if node pool down we re-route traffic to cross-region or fallback model variant. Step 3: if KV cache missing, apply last checkpoint and serve at reduced throughput. Step 4: escalate to SRE on-call if ack not within 10 min.
[06:50] Priya: do you maintain separate runbooks for data-plane vs control-plane failures?
[07:00] Omar: yes, control-plane (orchestration, API) vs data-plane (inference tensors, caches) have distinct playbooks. Control plane can be routed to our control-plane failover region; data plane requires instance rebuild/restore.
[07:20] Maya: I want to call out that for Dedicated customers we can set up cold or warm standby clusters in a second region and agree on failover SLAs in contract.
[07:35] Sarah: ok let's talk numbers again — you said hosted SLA 99.9. what's the credit model?
[07:45] Maya: Hosted has 99.9% with standard credit tiers; Dedicated commits can be pushed to 99.95 or 99.97 depending on capacity and contract. credits scale with outage duration, we'll include the precise schedule in the contract addendum.
[08:05] Ben: any exceptions? force majeure? regulatory maintenance windows?
[08:12] Maya: standard carve-outs exist; scheduled maintenance windows are announced and excluded from SLA. emergency maintenance for security vulnerabilities might be discussed case-by-case.
[08:25] Daniel: third-party dependencies — if your cloud region has outage (provider outage), how does Redwood handle it?
[08:34] Omar: multi-region redundancy and smart routing can failover across regions. For hosted customers we do cross-region failover; for Dedicated we recommend a hot-standby region. in extreme provider outage, we can route to an alternate region or to a downgraded model variant to preserve availability.
[08:58] [09:00] Sarah: are there drill options — tabletop exercises?
[09:05] Janelle: yes, Redwood runs tabletop incident drills and can facilitate a 60-90m exercise with Lakeside's Sec and Ops — we'll run detection scenarios and go through runbook steps.
[09:20] Priya: we want to test recovery times end-to-end; include priming caches in the test scope.
[09:28] Omar: acknowledged - we'll include cache priming scripts and telemetry checks.
[09:40] Daniel: one more: audit and egress — we need to ensure all data exfil attempts are logged and we get SIEM hooks.
[09:48] Omar: we export security events to your SIEM; also support syslog/forwarders and can send alerts to PagerDuty.
[10:00] Sarah: can Redwood sign our vendor addendum for data residency? we have EU customer flows that must remain in-region.
[10:10] Maya: yes, for data residency we support region pinning for deployments; Dedicated and Private let you keep data in-region. We'll include SLA language on region residency.
[10:25] Ben: liability caps? we'll review with legal.
[10:30] Maya: understood — we'll attach a standard addendum for review.
[10:40] [Speaker 2]: (brief crosstalk) can we see sample audit logs?
[10:48] Omar: yes, sample logs included in pack — shows request id, user, model, tokens consumed, key usage, and admin changes.
[11:00] Sarah: ok, let's get tactical — what's the plan to get us to a pilot with Dedicated capacity?
[11:10] Maya: propose pilot scope: 4-week trial, Dedicated pool in us-east and warm standby in us-west, simulate mixed workloads, run two incident drills, measure RTO/RPO and token-cost metrics. We'll provide a quote and contract terms.
[11:30] Priya: cost sensitivity — if we go Dedicated for pilot, will pricing include the warm standby?
[11:37] Maya: pilot pricing options: reserved pilot (discounted committed) or on-demand with additional warm standby fees. we'll propose both.
[11:50] Daniel: final ask — we need a clear escalation matrix with names/roles/emails and 24/7 numbers for Sev1.
[11:58] Omar: we'll include a sample escalation matrix; production version will be updated after contracting (with names and rotations).
[12:10] Maya: recap — action items: Maya send security pack (SOC2, ISO, diagrams), Omar share BCDR runbook + escalation matrix, schedule tabletop drill. any objections?
[12:25] Sarah: no objections, sounds good. Ben will review legal addendum.
[12:35] Priya: thanks, we'll prepare internal stakeholders.
[12:40] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and proposed dates.

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker labels and product names may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., K-V cache instead of KV cache, Redwood product names may be shortened).
